subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Chest pain and shortness of breath after a fall.
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 58 years old, male. I came in because I fell down outside, had some chest pain, and then I started feeling short of breath. I didn't think much of it at first, but then I ended up in the emergency room. Doctor: Can you describe the nature, location, duration, and intensity of the chest pain you experienced after the fall? Did it radiate anywhere, and was it associated with any other symptoms such as sweating, nausea, or dizziness? Patient: The chest pain was more of a pressure feeling, kind of in the middle of my chest, and it lasted maybe a few minutes. It didn't really radiate anywhere, and I didn't have any sweating or nausea, just some shortness of breath after it. Doctor: Could you provide details about the mechanism of the fall, such as the height from which you fell, whether you hit the ground directly on your chest or back, and if there was any immediate loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing at the time of the fall? Patient: I wasn't really paying attention to how I fell, to be honest. I was just walking and then I tripped. I don't think I hit my chest or back directly, and I didn't pass out or anything. I just kept going until I started feeling out of breath. Doctor: Can you describe the exact location, intensity, and duration of the chest pain? Have you noticed any changes in the pattern of your shortness of breath since the fall? Patient: The chest pain was more of a pressure feeling, kind of in the middle of my chest, and it lasted maybe a few minutes. I didn't have any changes in my shortness of breath really, just that I was out of breath a little bit after the fall, but I just walked it off. Doctor: Could you please provide details about any prior cardiac evaluations, such as ECGs, stress tests, or echocardiograms, even if they were

reference_so.subjective:
Basic information: 58-year-old male presenting with chest pain and shortness of breath following a fall

History of present illness: Onset of chest pain and shortness of breath after a fall, leading to emergency room admission. The chest pain was described as a pressure feeling in the middle of the chest, lasting a few minutes, without radiation, sweating, or nausea, accompanied by shortness of breath. The patient tripped and fell, not recalling the exact mechanism of injury, and did not hit his chest or back directly. He did not lose consciousness and continued walking until he started feeling out of breath. No swelling or bruising on chest or back noted post-fall. Shortness of breath resolved with walking. No palpitations, dizziness, or syncope reported. No prior cardiac conditions reported. No history of coronary artery disease, heart attack, or arrhythmias. No prior cardiac evaluations or imaging mentioned. The patient was not specifically evaluated for thoracic spine or chest injuries during the ER visit.

Past history: No prior cardiac conditions reported. No history of coronary artery disease, heart attack, or arrhythmias. No prior cardiac evaluations or imaging mentioned. The patient is aware of having hypertension.
